title: It’s Déjà Vu All Over Again: The Parallels of AI and Globalization | Council on Foreign Relations
gist: CFR president Michael Froman argues the public backlash to AI, ignited by Dario Amodei's essay urging leading labs to pace frontier development, mirrors the populist backlash to globalization: job-loss fears, concentrated and invisible benefits, loss of agency, and a sense of inevitability. He argues AI can avoid globalization's political fate only through serious worker-transition policy, a coherent federal stance, and US-led international standards, including with China.

insights.claim: An essay by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calling for leading labs to pace frontier AI development became the most dominant AI news story since ChatGPT's late-2022 launch, drawing responses from Bernie Sanders, Donald Trump, the Chinese Communist Party and top global CEOs.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: AI-safety/pacing narratives have gone mainstream; regulatory and political risk premia on frontier-lab valuations and AI capex names can reprice on a single policy essay.
insights.quote: Not since OpenAI’s rollout of ChatGPT in late 2022 has a single piece of AI news so dominated the headlines
insights.locator: The slow-burning crisis over the risks

insights.claim: Public anxiety about AI now spans data-center strain on water and energy supplies, job displacement, and machines that may out-think humans, and has spread nationally beyond the Bay Area.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Local opposition to data centers over water/power is a siting and permitting risk for hyperscaler buildouts and utilities.
insights.locator: This national conversation around the downside risks

insights.claim: Researcher statements putting existential risk from AI at around 10 percent, plus recent incidents of rogue AI agents hacking the internet, have pushed AI anxiety to a new level even though labor displacement has largely not yet materialized.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Anxiety is running ahead of measurable labor impact, so sentiment-driven policy shocks may precede economic data.
insights.locator: The debate is not new

insights.claim: The benefits side of AI, such as medical research and personalized learning, is almost absent from the current public debate.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: A one-sided narrative raises the odds of restrictive policy; watch for industry pivots to benefit messaging in health and education.
insights.locator: Almost absent from the debate

insights.claim: Like globalization, AI triggers fears of major job loss that aggregate-benefit arguments fail to dispel for those directly displaced.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Expect AI to become a trade-style political issue where aggregate GDP arguments lose to concentrated local losses.
insights.locator: First and foremost, both globalization and AI

insights.claim: The AI-optimist vision of abundance, where productivity makes work superfluous and people live on universal basic income, is politically unconvincing because people derive meaning and purpose from work; it fuels anxiety rather than easing it.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: UBI-style framing by AI boosters is likely to amplify rather than defuse backlash; policy will favor job-preserving/transition measures.
insights.quote: the notion of a life playing video games and cashing universal basic income checks simply does not resonate with most people
insights.locator: This vision of utopia offered by AI optimists

insights.claim: Globalization's consumer-price benefits were broadly shared but unequal and invisible, while its gains were perceived to flow to large firms, investors and a narrow elite; the same perception is already forming around AI.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Invisible diffuse benefits vs visible concentrated gains is a recipe for populist policy; AI winners face windfall-tax, antitrust and regulatory risk.
insights.quote: No one walked out of Walmart exclaiming, “Thank goodness for globalization!”
insights.locator: One of the challenges with globalization

insights.claim: With trillions of dollars pouring into AI, a handful of individuals and companies are being enriched years or decades before broad productivity gains reach the wider country, creating a timing gap between billionaire creation and public benefit.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: The lag between capex-driven wealth concentration and diffuse productivity gains is the political vulnerability window for AI incumbents.
insights.quote: The productivity boom that AI proponents promise will benefit every American will be years, if not decades, behind the minting of more billionaires in San Francisco.
insights.locator: But in the case of AI, trillions of dollars

insights.claim: Even if AI makes the nation more prosperous overall, perceived concentration of benefits will make it hard to build the popular buy-in needed for those gains to be politically sustainable.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Durability of pro-AI policy depends on visible distribution; watch for redistribution proposals tied to AI profits.
insights.locator: It is possible that the rapid development

insights.claim: Both globalization and AI reduce individuals' sense of agency: globalization replaced familiar local suppliers with diffuse global supply chains controlled by distant decision-makers, and part of its opposition is a desire to take back control.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: 'Take back control' politics that drove trade policy can be expected to extend to AI.
insights.locator: Beyond pure economics, both globalization and AI

insights.claim: AI intensifies the agency problem because neural networks are black boxes whose reasoning even experts cannot explain, meaning society is handing control of large parts of life and the economy to an unintelligible system.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Interpretability and explainability requirements are a plausible regulatory vector; interpretability tooling may gain policy tailwinds.
insights.quote: we are talking about handing over control of huge swaths of our lives and our economy to a system that is fundamentally impenetrable and unintelligible
insights.locator: With AI, this is perhaps even more true

insights.claim: Globalization was driven more by technology—the shipping container and broadband—than by trade policy, and efficiency incentives are only now being balanced against national security, resilience and supply-chain diversification.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Supports the view that the AI trend is technology-led and policy can shape but not stop it; resilience/diversification remains a structural theme.
insights.locator: Finally, there is something similar in the sense of inevitability

insights.claim: The productivity drive, rapid capability gains, potential recursive self-improvement, and multidimensional competition with China create a sense of inevitability around AI similar to globalization.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: China competition limits how far Washington will slow AI, capping the downside of domestic pacing movements.
insights.locator: We are hearing similar echoes with AI

insights.claim: Opposition to AI, like opposition to globalization, is populist and cuts across party lines: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon, who agree on little besides globalization, met to discuss slowing AI progress.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: A left-right populist coalition against AI makes restrictive legislation more plausible than partisan math suggests.
insights.locator: The most obvious similarity between the anger toward AI

insights.claim: Elites in both parties wrongly believe that better explaining AI's benefits would prevent backlash, repeating a globalization-era mistake.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Don't expect PR campaigns to defuse AI backlash; price in continued political friction.
insights.locator: At the same time, elites in both parties

themes.theme: Policy fixes to avoid globalization's fate

insights.claim: The response to globalization's worker displacement was inadequate, and today there is too much hand-wringing about AI and too little concrete work supporting worker transition.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Worker-transition programs (reskilling, education) are an underbuilt policy space likely to attract funding and mandates.
insights.quote: there is too much admiring of the problem and hand-wringing about AI, but far too little actual work being done to find and support solutions
insights.locator: First, if AI is going to avoid

insights.claim: RAISE US, a new bipartisan nonprofit led by former Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo and former Indiana Governor Eric Holcomb, is a notable exception focused on helping Americans transition to the AI economy.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Track RAISE US as a potential template for bipartisan AI workforce policy.
insights.locator: There is one notable exception

insights.claim: Trump's broad tariffs are a grand experiment in whether trade policy can reindustrialize the U.S. economy.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Reindustrialization outcomes from tariffs remain unproven; industrial and trade-exposed sectors hinge on the experiment's results.
insights.quote: With the broad application of tariffs, we are engaged in a grand experiment
insights.locator: Second, there is the role of the federal government

insights.claim: U.S. federal AI policy has been inconsistent, oscillating between laissez-faire and intervention such as model review and approval or taking equity stakes and revenue shares in specific companies.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Policy whiplash—including possible government equity/revenue stakes—is a key idiosyncratic risk for AI company investors.
insights.quote: the government has been schizophrenic about whether to let technology march ahead unimpeded or insert itself in the review and approval of models
insights.locator: When it comes to AI, the government has been schizophrenic

insights.claim: AI would benefit from US-led international standards, but competition with China—to reach superintelligence first or to control global diffusion of tech stacks—means the U.S. cannot afford to slow down until safety and alignment are solved.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: China rivalry puts a floor under U.S. AI investment and argues against a hard domestic pause.
insights.quote: Were the United States not engaged in a competition with China
insights.locator: Finally, as with global trade

insights.claim: The Biden administration, after considerable effort, reached agreement with China on keeping humans in the loop for nuclear weapons deployment, showing narrow US-China AI accords are possible but hard.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Precedent for targeted US-China AI risk agreements; incremental rather than sweeping deals are the base case.
insights.locator: After a lot of effort, the Biden administration

insights.claim: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is set to meet his Chinese counterpart in New York to discuss issues including AI cooperation, which could begin broader US-China AI dialogue.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Watch Bessent-China talks for AI cooperation signals that could ease export-control or tech-decoupling risk.
